fields.Front: Define a protocol (the three things it specifies).
fields.Back: A protocol defines the FORMAT and the ORDER of messages sent and received among network entities, and the ACTIONS taken on message transmission, receipt, or other events.

fields.Text: A protocol defines the {{c1::format}} and {{c2::order}} of messages exchanged, and the {{c3::actions}} taken on transmission/receipt of a message or other event.

fields.Front: What are the four messages in the slide's Web protocol example (TCP + HTTP)?
fields.Back: 1) TCP connection request, 2) TCP connection response, 3) GET http://gaia.cs.umass.edu/kurose_ross, 4) <file> returned.

fields.Front: Why must two communicating entities run the same protocol?
fields.Back: If they run different protocols (different message formats, order, or actions) they cannot interoperate and no useful work is accomplished; all Internet communication is governed by protocols.
